tour.label: Knotra tour
tour.settings.title: Learn to use Knotra
tour.settings.description: Build a small learning pipeline and learn to edit, connect and run its blocks.
tour.run.title: Run when you are ready
tour.run.description: Start your local engine in Settings when you are ready; it will start automatically on later app launches. Then return here, choose Run, check the question and local execution profile, and select Start run. If you skipped setup, continue the tour without executing anything.
tour.storageUnavailable: The tour is closed, but its dismissal could not be saved. It may appear again on your next launch.
library.research.description: Gather sources, draft a brief, request a human review and publish a Markdown file.
tour.welcome.title: Build your first pipeline
tour.welcome.description: Start with one model block, then add a human review and connect the steps. This short lesson creates one small pipeline you can keep and edit. Nothing runs until you choose to start it.
tour.rebuildLesson: Your edited pipeline no longer has the starting model block and connection used by this lesson. Create a fresh learning pipeline to practice again. Your existing pipeline and its edits stay unchanged.
tour.prompt.title: Give the model a task
tour.prompt.description: This block receives a question and produces text. Change its Instructions to ask for a short answer in your own style, then click outside the field to apply it. The canvas and Code are two views of the same workflow.
tour.add.title: Add a human review
tour.add.description: Choose Add node, then Human review. A human block pauses a real run so a person can read the model’s answer and respond. For this lesson, its draft input is ready for you to connect.
tour.connect.title: Connect the two steps
tour.connect.description: Click the text output on answer, then the draft input on human, or drag between them. The line passes the model’s answer into the review and sets the order. Add your own inputs and outputs in each block’s Inputs & outputs panel.
tour.review.title: Read, review and continue
tour.review.description: A human review pauses the pipeline until you respond. Open its request, read What to do and the draft under From previous steps, then write Your answer and choose Submit response. The pipeline continues with your reply. Open Runs to inspect the completed steps and outputs.
tour.pipeline.title: My first pipeline
tour.pipeline.description: Ask a question, then add and connect a human review.
tour.pipeline.question: What can I use Knotra for?
tour.pipeline.prompt: Answer the supplied question in one short paragraph. Return your answer in the text output.
tour.pipeline.reviewPrompt: Read the draft and share your feedback. Your answer will be saved with this run.
tour.models.title: Save a model source — or skip
tour.models.description: Add a named API connection, Codex, Claude, or local Ollama source. You can keep multiple sources and use different ones in each block. Your sources are restored after restart. This step does not start the engine; skip it to continue offline.
tour.binding.title: Choose a source and model for this block
tour.binding.description: In the answer block, choose a saved Source, then pick a Model from its list. Each model and agent block keeps its own choice. Use Manage model sources to refresh a source’s model list. If you skipped setup, continue the tour and connect a source later.

engineSetup.automatic: After its first setup, the engine starts automatically when you open Knotra. Stopping it keeps your sources and saved runs.
engineSetup.noSources: Save a model source or MCP server before starting the local engine.
engineSetup.restartRequired: Model sources changed. Restart the local engine to apply them; active runs will not be interrupted automatically.
editor.descriptionHelp: A note for people reading the workflow. It does not affect execution.
editor.taskHelp: The task sent to the model. Connected input data is added automatically. Describe the result you want.
editor.humanRequestHelp: The person sees this request and the connected inputs. Tell them what to check and what answer to give.
editor.promptFileHelp: Use a text file from this package instead of typing here. Only declared, nonempty UTF-8 files up to 1 MiB are listed.
editor.systemInstructionsHelp: Optional rules sent before the task, such as writing style or constraints. Input data still arrives separately.
editor.sandboxHelp: The isolated environment used for code and file tools. Choose a sandbox available in this workflow.
editor.mcpServerHelp: The connection that provides the tool. Choose its tool name below.
editor.modelAliasHelp: An internal name shared by blocks using this binding. Choosing another alias reuses its settings. Use Source and Model above to change only this block.
editor.toolArgumentsHelp: The named values sent to the tool. Use fixed values for constant settings, or an expression to pass this block’s inputs.
editor.toolBindingHelp: This tool uses an existing data mapping. Keep one selector: from, value, expr, or coalesce. A path selects part of a from result.
editor.toolResponseHelp: Structured data returns the tool’s structured result. Content blocks returns its raw response blocks. This must match the result output’s schema.
editor.commandArgumentsHelp: Each field is one argument passed to the executable, in order. For example: python, then -c, then the script.
editor.modelParametersHelp: Optional provider settings, such as temperature for response variation or an output limit. Supported names depend on the provider and model. Leave empty to inherit the source defaults.
editor.accountParametersHelp: Account sources do not accept API parameters. Use source defaults to remove them from this block.
editor.blockPurpose.llm: Give a model a task, then choose the model to answer it. Connect the data it needs in Inputs & outputs.
editor.blockPurpose.agent: Give the agent a task. It can call the model and permitted tools repeatedly, within the step limit.
editor.blockPurpose.human: Pause the run for a person. They read your request and connected inputs, then return the answer defined in Outputs.
editor.blockPurpose.code: Run a command in a sandbox. Choose the executable and its arguments, then define the data and files it receives or returns.
editor.blockPurpose.tool: Call one tool from an MCP server. Choose the tool and the named arguments to send it.
editor.blockPurpose.switch: Choose a route by checking conditions in order. The first matching route wins; the default is used if none match.
editor.blockPurpose.foreach: Run the inner graph once for each item in a list. Choose the list input and how many items can run at the same time.
editor.blockPurpose.loop: Repeat the inner graph until the stop condition is true or the iteration limit is reached.
editor.blockPurpose.pipeline: Run another pipeline from this package. Choose its file and the resources it is allowed to use.
resources.existingEngineHelp: Connect to an engine you already run on this computer or another server. Its own model sources and runtime settings stay under its control.
resources.existingEngineTokenHelp: Required for remote engines. Local loopback addresses can connect without a token. Tokens are used for this session and are not included in workspace backups.
engineSetup.sourcesPending: Connection changes are saved. They will apply automatically after all running, paused and waiting workflows finish.
engineSetup.sourcesApplying: Applying connections. The local engine will be ready again shortly.
engineSetup.sourcesFailed: Could not finish applying connections. Knotra will retry automatically.
timeline.title: Pipeline activity
timeline.empty: No activity has been received yet. Events will appear here as the pipeline runs.
timeline.recent: Recent received activity. Open Replay to explore the saved execution history.
resources.chooseConnectionsInSteps: Choose these connections when setting up a pipeline step.
resources.forSecretInputs: Supplies a secret value to pipeline steps.
resources.connectionsCheckedOnRun: Connections are checked when you run a pipeline.
resources.engineConnectionsEmpty: This engine has no configured model sources or tools.
mcpSetup.title: MCP servers
mcpSetup.intro: Connect a server once, then choose its tools in Tool and AI agent blocks.
mcpSetup.empty: No MCP servers added yet. Connect a server to give your pipelines access to its tools.
mcpSetup.desktopOnly: Add MCP servers in the desktop app. An existing engine uses its own configured servers.
mcpSetup.name: Server name
mcpSetup.urlHelp: Use the server’s MCP endpoint over HTTPS, or HTTP on localhost. Enter tokens separately; URL parameters are not supported.
mcpSetup.tokenHelp: Paste the token without the Bearer prefix if the server requires one. It is kept in your system credential store.
mcpSetup.tokenKeep: Leave blank to keep the saved token. Enter a new token to replace it.
mcpSetup.tokenNewAddress: For a new address, re-enter the token or choose Remove saved token.
mcpSetup.toolsHelp: Choose which tools can be used in your pipelines. New tools stay disabled until you enable them.
mcpSetup.noTools: This server did not expose any tools. Check the endpoint or server configuration.
mcpSetup.missingTools: Some enabled tools are no longer advertised by this server.
editor.mcpNotConnected: Add an MCP server in Settings to use its tools here.
editor.agentMcpHelp: Choose the tools this agent may use. It decides when to call them.
editor.toolNotAllowed: Enable this tool in Settings before using it.
editor.toolNoArguments: This tool does not need arguments.
editor.unsupportedToolArguments: This tool does not accept these saved fields: {names}.
editor.mcpContentResponseHelp: This tool returns content blocks. Use that format for this block’s result.
editor.mcpStructuredResponseHelp: This tool returns structured data. Use its published result schema.
editor.sandboxEnvironmentHelp: The isolated environment where this block runs commands and works with files.
editor.noSandboxEnvironments: Start or connect an engine in Settings to see its available code environments.
editor.sandboxUnavailable: This environment is not available on the connected engine. Choose another environment or check engine setup.
editor.sandboxOffline: Saved environment. Connect the engine to check its availability before running.
editor.sandboxSelectedHelp: Choose Python for Python scripts or Node.js for JavaScript. Other environments come from your engine configuration.
editor.sandboxPermissionsHelp: Allow this agent to read files, write files, or run commands in its selected environment.
resources.connectionsForPipeline: Connections used by {name}. Choose them separately for each block.
resources.modelsHelp: Add an API, Codex, Claude, or Ollama source in Settings. Then choose a source and model in each Model or AI agent block.
resources.mcpHelp: Add an MCP server and enable its tools in Settings. Choose a tool in a Tool block, or grant tools to an AI agent.
resources.sandboxesHelp: Code environments run scripts and provide file tools. Start or connect an engine in Settings, then choose an environment in each Code or AI agent block.
resources.secretsHelp: Secret values are configured on the engine. Pipelines store references only; they do not contain the values.
resources.chooseInBlock: Not set up — choose in this block
resources.selectPipeline: Open or create a pipeline to see the connections used by its blocks.
resources.aliasExplanation: Names such as “writer” are internal links in the pipeline file. Knotra creates them when you choose a connection in a block. Editing a shared binding here affects every block using it.
resources.savedSelectionOffline: Saved selection. Connect the engine to check availability.
resources.savedSelectionUnavailable: This saved selection is unavailable on the connected engine. Choose another connection or check Settings.
desktopControl.title: Control Knotra with MCP
desktopControl.help: Connect an assistant to create and edit pipelines, manage sources, run workflows, and answer human requests. Its changes appear in this app.
desktopControl.appOpen: Keep Knotra open while using its MCP tools. Connections use a local, authenticated bridge; saved credentials are never returned to the assistant.
desktopControl.configurationHelp: Add this server to your assistant’s MCP configuration, then connect it. The pipeline schema and authoring guide are included as MCP resources.
desktopControl.copyHelp: Select the configuration above and copy it with your keyboard.
